label: Digitally Immersed & Emotionally Strained
summary: This profile represents highly educated women who spend substantial time on social media (averaging nearly 4 hours daily, with many exceeding 5 hours) and report elevated levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety. Across all three psychological distress measures—loneliness (UCLA-8 mean 1.78), depression (PHQ-9 mean 1.81), and anxiety (GAD-7 mean 2.27)—scores are consistently above moderate thresholds, with anxiety being the most pronounced. The combination of heavy social-media engagement and heightened emotional distress distinguishes this group from other respondent clusters.
demographic_anchor: Female, graduate-level education or above, daily social-media use exceeding 5 hours
behavior_markers: Heavy daily social-media consumption averaging approximately 3.9 hours with a substantial proportion exceeding 5 hours
Elevated loneliness scores suggesting persistent feelings of social disconnection
Moderate-to-high depressive symptom severity on the PHQ-9
Notably high anxiety symptoms, the most elevated distress indicator in this profile
High educational attainment paired with significant psychological distress
tone: Concerned and empathetic, highlighting the co-occurrence of heavy digital engagement and emotional vulnerability

label: Well-Adjusted Light-Use Graduate Male
summary: This profile represents male respondents with graduate-level education who report lower loneliness, lower depressive symptoms, and lower anxiety compared to other groups. They engage in relatively light daily social-media use, averaging roughly 1–3 hours per day. Their psychological well-being indicators are consistently favorable, with notably low scores on standardized measures of loneliness (UCLA-8), depression (PHQ-9), and anxiety (GAD-7).
demographic_anchor: Male, graduate degree or above, 1–3 hours of daily social-media use
behavior_markers: Light social-media usage averaging approximately 2.8 hours per day
Low self-reported loneliness (UCLA-8 mean ≈ 0.78)
Minimal depressive symptomatology (PHQ-9 mean ≈ 0.27)
Near-floor anxiety levels (GAD-7 mean ≈ 0.03)
Pattern consistent with balanced digital engagement without psychological distress

label: Lonely but Low-Distress Heavy Social-Media User
summary: This profile captures highly educated women who report elevated loneliness yet comparatively low levels of depressive and anxiety symptoms, despite spending nearly five hours per day on social media. Their loneliness scores stand above average while their depression and anxiety remain subdued, suggesting that heavy social-media engagement may coexist with social disconnection without necessarily escalating into clinical-level mood or anxiety disturbance.
demographic_anchor: Female, graduate-level education or above, approximately 3–5 hours of daily social-media use
behavior_markers: Elevated loneliness (UCLA-8 mean ≈ 1.30) relative to other profiles
Lower depressive symptomatology (PHQ-9 mean ≈ 0.90)
Lower anxiety symptomatology (GAD-7 mean ≈ 0.85)
Heavy daily social-media use averaging close to 5 hours (midpoint ≈ 4.89 hours)
Possible pattern of using social media as a substitute for in-person social connection
tone: Reflective and mildly disconnected; outwardly functional with an undercurrent of social isolation

label: Well-Adjusted Graduate Male with Light Social-Media Use
summary: This profile represents a group of 217 respondents characterized by notably low levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety symptoms, combined with relatively light daily social-media use averaging roughly 1.6 hours. Their mean scores on the UCLA-8 loneliness scale (1.22), PHQ-9 depression scale (0.82), and GAD-7 anxiety scale (0.90) all fall well below clinical thresholds, suggesting generally positive psychological well-being. These individuals tend to be highly educated males who maintain a moderate and controlled relationship with social media.
demographic_anchor: Male, graduate-level education or above, reporting 1–3 hours of daily social-media use
behavior_markers: Light daily social-media use averaging approximately 1.6 hours
Loneliness scores well below scale midpoints (UCLA-8 mean: 1.22)
Minimal depressive symptomatology (PHQ-9 mean: 0.82)
Low anxiety symptom levels (GAD-7 mean: 0.90)
Controlled and moderate engagement with digital platforms rather than heavy or compulsive use
